back: A method of deciding whether a project is worthwhile by listing, valuing and comparing all its costs and benefits, including social ones.
Net benefit = total benefits − total costs. Worthwhile if positive.
Benefit-cost ratio = total benefits ÷ total costs. Worthwhile if above 1.

front: Economic and social costs and benefits
back: Economic: money costs and benefits to the organisation. Social: effects on the community and environment such as pollution, congestion, jobs and health.
Whole-community view, forces a full list of effects, common measure in money, easier to justify decisions.
Social effects are hard to value, forecasts are uncertain, timing and discounting, hidden winners and losers, possible bias, can be costly.
Reducing the value of future costs and benefits because money received later is worth less than money today.
Define the project, list costs, list benefits, value each in money, add up, compare, then test the result with different assumptions.
